analysis.investment_thesis: Crompton is a decent consumer electricals franchise with ROIC of ~24% (EBIT 888 Cr / invested capital ~3,674 Cr), but the earnings yield is only ~5.1% (EBIT 888 Cr / EV ~17,363 Cr), well below the Magic Formula's 6% threshold. The stock is a quality business priced for quality — exactly the kind of situation the formula tells you to pass on until price corrects.
key_strengths: ROIC ~24% demonstrates genuine capital efficiency in a competitive consumer durables market
Near-zero leverage (D/E 0.05) and 5/5 years of positive OCF show financial discipline post-Butterfly acquisition debt paydown
Revenue CAGR of 9.8% and EBITDA of 8.3% over 7 years show steady, if unspectacular, compounding
key_risks: Earnings yield of ~5.1% (EV/EBIT ~19.5x) is below the Magic Formula's minimum attractiveness threshold
Net profit peaked at 617 Cr in FY21 and only recovered to 564 Cr in FY25, suggesting the Butterfly acquisition diluted earnings quality
Operating margins are thin at ~8% — any input cost spike (copper, aluminum) can significantly dent profitability
red_flags: Finance costs spiked from 35 Cr (FY22) to 109 Cr (FY23) — the Butterfly acquisition loaded debt that is now being paid down but hurt earnings for 3 years
Net profit CAGR of 8.2% over 7 years is actually lower than revenue CAGR of 9.8% — margins are structurally compressing
analysis.detailed_analysis: Using FY2025 numbers: EBIT = 888 Cr, EV = Market Cap (17,088) + Net Debt (479 - 204) = ~17,363 Cr, giving Earnings Yield of 5.1%. Capital employed (equity 3,399 + debt 479 - cash 204) = ~3,674 Cr implies ROIC of ~24%, confirmed by the company-reported ROCE of 19%. The Magic Formula requires BOTH metrics to be attractive — Crompton clears the ROIC bar but fails on earnings yield at this price. The EV/EBITDA of 22.65x and P/E of 34x reflect that the market already prices in quality. Crompton is a Hold, not a Buy — I'd need the earnings yield to reach 10%+ (implying price around 130-140) to get excited.
